Build a spatial frame

Source: R/frame.R
areal_frame.Rd

A frame is the set of areal units the model is defined on, with their adjacency graph and any groupings to aggregate predictions to (regions, countries, ...). Build it either from polygons, in which case adjacency is computed and survey coordinates can later be assigned to units, or from a ready-made adjacency matrix.

Usage

areal_frame(
  polygons = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  adjacency = NULL,
  ids = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  queen = TRUE,
  link_islands = TRUE,
  link_within = NULL,
  link_crs = NULL,
  adjacency_snap = 0,
  link_simplify = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

polygons

An sf object with one row per areal unit (POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON). Units are taken in row order. Needs the sf and spdep packages.

id

For polygons: the name of the column holding unique unit ids.

adjacency

Instead of polygons: a square, symmetric 0/1 matrix (base or Matrix) with zero diagonal, one row per unit.

ids

For adjacency: unique unit ids, in row order. Defaults to the row names of adjacency, or 1..m.

groups

Groupings of the units, for aggregating predictions. For polygons: names of columns of polygons. If the vector is named, the names become the group names (e.g. c(region = "NAME_1", country = "GID_0")). For adjacency: a data frame with one row per unit in row order, one column per grouping. Grouping names become column names of the prediction tables, so names the package uses there are refused (id, area, t, time, y, k, mean, sd, ...).

queen

For polygons: units sharing only a corner are neighbours (TRUE, queen) or not (FALSE, rook).

link_islands

For polygons: join disconnected components to the largest one (see Details).

link_within

For polygons: the name of a grouping inside which island links are made where possible, or NULL.

link_crs

The projected coordinate reference system in which distances are measured. It is used for island links here, and for snapping survey points in areal_data(). Its units must be metres. The default is the projection of polygons if they are projected in metres (and not Web Mercator), and otherwise a Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on the units (allowing for frames that cross the 180th meridian). For a frame spanning a large part of the globe, give a suitable projection here.

adjacency_snap

For polygons: units whose borders come within this distance (metres, measured in link_crs) count as neighbours. The default, 0, needs shared borders to match exactly, as they do within one boundary file. Boundaries assembled from several sources (e.g. one file per country) rarely meet exactly at national borders: a snap of 1-2 km joins them.

link_simplify

Tolerance (in link_crs units) used to simplify polygons before measuring island-link distances, which is much faster. A unit that vanishes when simplified keeps its full detail. The default is 1/10,000 of the diagonal of the bounding box. Use 0 for full detail.

verbose

Print progress messages.

Value

An object of class stareal_frame:

ids, m

unit ids (in unit order) and their number

W

sparse symmetric 0/1 adjacency, island links included

groups

data frame: id and one column per grouping

links

data frame of added island edges, or NULL

n_components

connected components of the final graph

eig

eigendecomposition of the Laplacian: values, vectors

polygons

the sf polygons (id and grouping columns), or NULL

crs_planar

the projection used for distances, or NULL

source

what the frame was built from

Details

The spatial prior is a Leroux conditional autoregressive model on the graph, which uses the eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian \(R = D - W\). It is computed once here. It is a dense \(m \times m\) problem, and takes about a minute for a few thousand units with an optimised BLAS.

Islands. A graph in several pieces leaves each piece without neighbours to borrow strength from. With polygons and link_islands = TRUE (the default), every component other than the largest is joined to it by one edge. The edge runs from the component's unit closest to the main component to the closest unit of the main component, by polygon distance. If link_within names a grouping, that unit is looked for first among main-component units in the same group (e.g. the same country), and elsewhere only if the group has none. The added edges are listed in $links. A frame built from an adjacency matrix cannot be linked like this, and a disconnected one is accepted with a warning.

Save the frame. Build a frame once and save it (saveRDS()): the eigendecomposition is the slow step, and its eigenvectors depend on the BLAS library, so a frame rebuilt on another machine gives slightly different random draws for the same seed.

See also

areal_lattice() for a regular grid, areal_data() to attach survey data.

Examples

# from an adjacency matrix: four units in a line, two regions
W <- matrix(0, 4, 4)
W[cbind(1:3, 2:4)] <- 1
W <- W + t(W)
fr <- areal_frame(adjacency = W, ids = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
                  groups = data.frame(region = c("N", "N", "S", "S")))
#> eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian (m = 4)
fr
#> <stareal_frame> 4 units, 3 edges (mean 1.5 neighbours), 1 connected component
#>   built from: adjacency matrix (no polygons)
#>   groupings: region (2)
